title: 2026 U.S. Senate election in Michigan
description: The 2026 Michigan Senate election is an open-seat race for the seat held by retiring Democrat Gary Peters. Taking place in a state Donald Trump won by 1.4 points in 2024, it is one of only two Democratic-held Senate seats up in a Trump-won state and is rated a Toss Up by the Cook Political Report, making it a central battleground for control of the Senate. Democrats face a competitive August 4 primary among three candidates representing different party factions: U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens (the establishment-backed frontrunner), state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, and former Wayne County health director Abdul El-Sayed. Republicans have coalesced behind former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers, endorsed by Donald Trump, as they seek to win their first Michigan Senate race since 1994.

candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.summary: Abdul El-Sayed is a physician, epidemiologist, and former public health official from Michigan who is running for the U.S. Senate in 2026. He previously led the Detroit Health Department and later Wayne County’s Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services, and his campaign says he is focused on health care, affordability, civil rights, and government reform.

Healthcare.stance: El-Sayed supports Medicare for All and says health care should be guaranteed as a right. His campaign also says he wants to lower prescription drug costs and build a system that works for every American.

sources.title: A Healthier America
Dr. Abdul El-Sayed: “I’ve Worked to Expand Rx Kids. But We Still Need Medicare for All.”

Economy.stance: El-Sayed says he wants an economy for working people by ending corporate tax breaks, strengthening unions, supporting small businesses, and lowering costs for Michiganders. His campaign also emphasizes domestic manufacturing and public investment.

sources.title: An Economy for Working People
Abdul's Priorities

Climate/Energy.stance: El-Sayed says he wants stronger protections for clean air and water and to hold polluters accountable for contamination. He frames environmental policy as part of public health and environmental justice.

sources.title: Clean Air & Water

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: El-Sayed supports abortion rights and says he would codify the rights once protected by Roe v. Wade into federal law. His campaign also links reproductive access to broader civil rights and health care protections.

sources.title: Civil Rights & Liberties

Immigration.stance: El-Sayed has said he wants to abolish ICE and sharply limit its role, while still supporting immigration enforcement in a different form. He has criticized ICE as militarized and abusive.

sources.title: 6 major issues in Michigan’s US Senate race
Abdul El-Sayed – Michigan U.S. Senate Candidate 2026
Abdul's Priorities

Foreign Policy.stance: El-Sayed says he favors a diplomacy-first foreign policy rooted in multilateralism, human rights, and alliances. He opposes direct funding of foreign militaries and says the U.S. should avoid interventions like Vietnam or Iraq.

sources.title: Sensible Foreign Policy

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: El-Sayed says he will protect civil rights and liberties for people regardless of race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or income. His campaign emphasizes equal rights, non-discrimination protections, and the right to protest peacefully.

sources.title: Civil Rights & Liberties

Education.stance: El-Sayed supports universal pre-K, stronger public K-12 schools, school infrastructure investment, vocational training, and debt-free or tuition-free paths to higher education. He also says he wants more funding for research and higher education.

sources.title: More and Better Education, not Less

Tech & AI.stance: El-Sayed has proposed rules for data centers that would require them to pay for their own energy demand, provide community transparency, use binding community-benefits agreements, and meet environmental safeguards. He also ties developments to local jobs and apprenticeship requirements.

sources.title: Terms of Engagement for Data Centers
El-Sayed lays out policy 'terms of engagement' with AI data centers

Election Policy.stance: El-Sayed says he wants to get money out of politics and has supported ending the filibuster and reforming the Supreme Court. He frames these changes as ways to reduce corporate influence and improve democratic accountability.

sources.title: Must-win Michigan Senate race turns messy for Democrats amid fight over Israel and future of the party
Abdul El-Sayed courts college voters, controversy in Michigan Senate race

Local Issues.stance: El-Sayed’s data-center proposal says new projects should not raise rates for residents, should pay their own energy costs, and should include community input, closed-loop water systems, union labor, apprenticeship requirements, and penalties for noncompliance. The campaign presents the plan as a local affordability and infrastructure issue.

sources.title: Terms of Engagement for Data Centers
Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed presents 'terms of engagement' for data centers

candidates.name: Mallory McMorrow
candidates.summary: Mallory McMorrow is a Michigan state senator and Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in 2026. Her campaign says she is running to focus on affordability, democracy, and protecting rights and freedoms, and she has highlighted her legislative record on wages, gun safety, and reproductive rights.

summary_sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Healthcare.stance: McMorrow supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid, lowering prescription drug costs, and creating a public option so coverage is not tied to a job or marital status. Her campaign also says she wants to protect reproductive and mental health care as basic rights.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Economy.stance: McMorrow says she wants an economy that rewards work rather than wealth, including raising wages, cutting taxes for working families, ending the carried interest loophole, and supporting small businesses through credit, capital, and regulatory streamlining.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Climate/Energy.stance: McMorrow’s agenda calls for clean water, environmental protection, and energy policies that keep costs down while holding large users accountable. Her campaign also says she supports stronger oversight of data-center development, including renewable-energy requirements and protections for ratepayers.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate
Data Centers Done Right

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: McMorrow says she supports abortion access and broader reproductive health care protections, including paid family and medical leave, maternal health programs, birthing centers, doulas, and postpartum mental health support. Her campaign also highlights her support for taking Michigan’s Rx Kids program nationwide.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate
McMorrow Proposes a Better ‘Baby Bonus’ with National Cash Prescription Program for New Moms

Immigration.stance: McMorrow’s agenda calls for cracking down on fentanyl trafficking with stronger border enforcement and targeting the supply chain, while also expanding treatment and recovery services. Her campaign page also includes immigration and foreign policy as a combined issue area, but does not lay out a detailed immigration overhaul on the agenda page reviewed here.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: McMorrow supports universal background checks, a federal assault-weapons ban, a federal red-flag law modeled on Michigan’s, safe-storage laws, a ban on ghost guns, and repeal of PLCAA. Her campaign also says she wants more funding for local public safety and mental health crisis response.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Foreign Policy.stance: McMorrow’s agenda groups immigration and foreign policy together and emphasizes humanitarian considerations, but the campaign page reviewed here does not provide a detailed foreign-policy platform. Public reporting has also covered her comments on the Gaza-Israel war, but her campaign agenda itself is limited on this issue.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: McMorrow’s agenda emphasizes civil rights, privacy, voting rights, and support for underserved communities. Her campaign also frames its platform around equity, accountability, and community investment.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Education.stance: McMorrow supports making education more affordable, expanding child care and early childhood education, strengthening child labor protections, and increasing access to paid leave and child tax credits for families. Her campaign also says it wants to hold social media and tech companies accountable for harms to kids’ mental health.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Tech & AI.stance: McMorrow says social media and big tech companies should be held accountable for harms to children, and her agenda calls for stronger regulation to put kids’ well-being over profits. Her campaign also proposes guardrails for technology and innovation, including oversight of data-center development.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate
Data Centers Done Right

Election Policy.stance: McMorrow says democracy needs stronger accountability and supports reforms such as protecting voting rights and considering changes to the filibuster and Supreme Court structure. Her campaign also places transparency, accountability, and effectiveness among its core agenda areas.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate

Local Issues.stance: McMorrow’s local-issues agenda focuses heavily on Michigan-specific economic development, including data-center rules, small-business support, infrastructure costs, union labor, and protections for ratepayers and communities. Her campaign also highlights state-level track record items such as economic development reform and support for local redevelopment funding.

sources.title: Agenda — Mallory McMorrow for U.S. Senate
Data Centers Done Right

flags.concern: Career history shows Abdul El-Sayed as 'Public health professor' at University of Michigan (2017–2019), but also lists him as 'Executive Director' of Detroit Health Department (2015–2017). The overlapping timeline (2017 appears in both end_year and start_year) is ambiguous — it is unclear whether these roles were concurrent or sequential. The profile does not clarify if he held both positions simultaneously or transitioned between them in 2017.
flags.suggestion: Clarify the exact transition date between the Detroit Health Department role and the University of Michigan role. If concurrent, explicitly note that. If sequential, ensure the years do not overlap.

flags.concern: The donor summary states McMorrow 'has eschewed corporate PAC money in her Senate run, though her prior state Senate campaigns received donations from DTE Energy.' This is factually consistent with the cited sources, but the phrasing 'eschewed' (a positive-valence verb) contrasts with how El-Sayed's similar pledge is described as a straightforward 'pledge to accept no corporate PAC money.' Both candidates have similar donor profiles (high small-dollar, low PAC), but the language used to describe McMorrow's stance carries a slightly more active/principled tone. This is a minor asymmetry.
flags.suggestion: Use parallel language for both candidates' PAC pledges. For example, both could be described as 'pledging to reject corporate PAC contributions' or both as 'eschewing corporate PAC money.' Ensure the framing is symmetrical.

flags.concern: The Immigration stance for Haley Stevens states she 'introduced legislation to create independent oversight of DHS and ICE misconduct' and 'Her position appears to favor accountability and local coordination rather than abolishing ICE.' This is a reasonable inference from the cited sources, but the phrase 'rather than abolishing ICE' introduces a contrastive framing that is not explicitly stated in the sources reviewed. The sources show what Stevens *did* propose (oversight), but do not directly quote her rejecting abolition. This is a minor interpretive inference.
flags.suggestion: Rephrase to focus on what Stevens has affirmatively proposed (oversight, accountability, local coordination) without introducing the counterfactual 'rather than abolishing ICE' unless that is directly quoted or paraphrased from a source.

flags.concern: Rogers' Healthcare stance cites a Bridge Michigan article titled 'Senate hopeful Mike Rogers floats copays, high-risk pools for health care' and notes his opposition to extending ACA tax credits. The stance summary states he 'would roll back some Affordable Care Act provisions, including ending no-cost preventive care.' The phrase 'ending no-cost preventive care' is a strong characterization. The source headline uses 'floats' (tentative language), and the profile notes 'His campaign has also said it would release a fuller health care plan.' This suggests the proposals may not be finalized. The phrasing could be more cautious to reflect the tentative nature of the proposals.
flags.suggestion: Soften the language to reflect the tentative nature: e.g., 'has proposed changes that would reportedly roll back some ACA provisions' or 'has discussed proposals that would include...' to align with the source's use of 'floats.'

flags.concern: Rogers' Firearms stance is marked as 'low' confidence and states 'No public position found on election reform in the sources reviewed.' This appears to be a copy-paste error — the field is about Firearms & Second Amendment, not election reform. The stance correctly notes that Rogers' campaign materials do not lay out a detailed gun policy, but the error message is misaligned.
flags.suggestion: Correct the error message to read: 'No detailed public position found on firearms and Second Amendment issues in the sources reviewed.' Or simply remove the misaligned text and rely on the accurate stance description that follows.

flags.concern: Rogers' Election Policy stance is marked as 'low' confidence and states 'No public position found on election reform in the sources reviewed.' This is appropriate given the sources reviewed. However, the field label is 'Election Policy' (which typically includes voting rights, campaign finance, filibuster reform, etc.), and the absence of a position is correctly documented. No issue here, but noting for completeness.

Asymmetric framing on ICE policy: El-Sayed's stance states he 'wants to abolish ICE and sharply limit its role, while still supporting immigration enforcement in a different form. He has criticized ICE as militarized and abusive.' Stevens' stance states she 'introduced legislation to create independent oversight of DHS and ICE misconduct' and 'Her position appears to favor accountability and local coordination rather than abolishing ICE.' The framing of El-Sayed's position uses his own language ('abolish ICE') and includes his characterization ('militarized and abusive'), while Stevens' position is described in terms of what she *did* (introduced legislation) and what she *does not* support (abolition). This creates an asymmetry: El-Sayed's stance is presented through his own framing, while Stevens' is presented through a negative contrast. Both are sourced, but the presentation differs in tone.
flags.suggestion: Reframe both stances using parallel structure. For example: 'El-Sayed says he wants to abolish ICE and replace it with a different enforcement model, citing concerns about militarization and abuse. Stevens has introduced legislation for independent oversight of ICE and DHS misconduct, focusing on accountability and local coordination.' This presents both candidates' affirmative positions without asymmetric framing.
